title: Top positive distributions recover the Steinberg highest vector
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of prime characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected affine $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: it is smooth, connected and of finite type, has no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group scheme with finite central kernel to $S$ is an isomorphism. Solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes eventually become trivial; finite central means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq B\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B$. A split torus is a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$, with $\mathbf G_m(D)=D^\times$; maximal means maximal under inclusion; Borel means maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup. Its unipotent radical is its largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup, with unipotent meaning unipotent geometric matrices in a faithful representation. Use the character lattice $X^*(T)=\operatorname{Hom}(T,\mathbf G_m)$ and the positive roots $\Phi^+$ in the tangent space $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, with roots interpreted as torus characters, as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Put $N=|\Phi^+|$. Fix $r\ge1$ and $q=p^r$. For each affine $F$-group $K$, put $K^{(q)}=\operatorname{Spec}(F[K]\otimes_{F,a\mapsto a^q}F)$ and $K_r=\ker(F^r_{K/F}:K\to K^{(q)})$, where the relative Frobenius has coordinate map $c\otimes a\mapsto ac^q$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For a finite such kernel put $\operatorname{Dist}(K_r)=\operatorname{Hom}_F(F[K_r],F)$, with convolution product $(ab)(f)=(a\otimes b)(\Delta f)$, unit evaluation at the identity, augmentation $a\mapsto a(1)$ and antipode $\sigma$ dual to inversion; these agree with the finite-order distributions of [def-sfb-affine-group-distribution-calculus]. Assume $\rho\in X^*(T)$ satisfies $2\rho=\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$, and choose a $B$-character $\widetilde\rho$ extending it trivially on the unipotent radical. Put $\lambda=(q-1)\rho$ and $\widetilde\lambda=\widetilde\rho^{q-1}$. Choose an opposite Borel subgroup $B^-$, that is, a Borel subgroup $B^-\supseteq T$ with $B\cap B^-=T$, with unipotent radical $U^-$. Let $A=\operatorname{Dist}(S_r)$ and $D_B=\operatorname{Dist}(B_r)$. Let $F_\lambda$ be the one-dimensional $D_B$-module with action $b\cdot1=b(\widetilde\lambda|_{B_r})$, and define $M=A\otimes_{D_B}F_\lambda$ and $v=1\otimes1$, as in [lem-sfb-frobenius-kernel-induced-dual-pbw]. Choose any ordering $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_N$ of $\Phi^+$ and any root parametrizations $x_{\pm\alpha_i}:\mathbf G_a\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{\pm\alpha_i}$ [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. Let $d_{\pm\alpha_i}^{(n)}$ be coefficient extraction $f\mapsto[t^n]x_{\pm\alpha_i}^*f$ on the $r$th kernels for $0\le n<q$, regarded as elements of $A$. Put
$$e_{\rm top}=\prod_{i=1}^N d_{\alpha_i}^{(q-1)},\qquad f_{\rm top}=\prod_{i=1}^N d_{-\alpha_i}^{(q-1)}.$$
There exists $c\in F^\times$ such that $e_{\rm top}f_{\rm top}v=cv$ in $M$. For the empty root system the products and $c$ are $1$. The assertion holds for every prime $p$, including $2$, and every $r\ge1$.

source.place: Agent formulation of the top-root distribution calculation for the infinitesimal proof associated with Jantzen II.3.18. Local book WANTED. Kaneda, Section 2.5, equation (9), printed p.323, corroborates the resulting simplicity, not this calculation.

proof.text: If $N=0$, both specified products are $1$, so take $c=1$. For $N>0$, apply the current finite-kernel PBW statement with $\eta=\lambda$, $\widetilde\eta=\widetilde\lambda$ and the given opposite Borel $B^-$. The character $\widetilde\lambda=\widetilde\rho^{q-1}$ restricts to $\lambda$ on $T$ and is trivial on $R_u(B)$, as that statement requires. Its balanced tensor product $M_r(\lambda)=\operatorname{Dist}(S_r)\otimes_{\operatorname{Dist}(B_r)}F_\lambda$ is precisely $M$, with $v_\lambda=v$. Thus $S_r$ is finite and $v\ne0$. For every $b\in D_B$, the balancing relation gives $bv=1\otimes(b\cdot1)=b(\widetilde\lambda|_{B_r})v$. Hence the initial vector has exactly the $B_r$-eigencharacter required for step 3.

source.place: Agent argument from the balanced tensor product; finite-kernel PBW is the cited node, not a claim from Milne.

proof.text: Construct Borels $C_0=B,C_1,\ldots,C_N$ containing $T$, with positive systems $\Psi_j$ and $\rho_j=\frac12\sum_{\gamma\in\Psi_j}\gamma$, as follows. Whenever $\Psi_j\ne-\Phi^+$, some simple root $\beta_{j+1}$ of $\Psi_j$ belongs to $\Phi^+$: otherwise all simple roots are negative in the original base, so every root of $\Psi_j$, a nonnegative sum of them, is original-negative. Choose this $\beta_{j+1}$ and use the adjacent-Borel lemma's conjugate $C_{j+1}$. Its positive system deletes $\beta_{j+1}$ and adds $-\beta_{j+1}$. Thus $|\Psi_{j+1}\cap\Phi^+|=|\Psi_j\cap\Phi^+|-1$. After precisely $N$ steps the chosen $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_N$ enumerate $\Phi^+$ without repetitions. Moreover $\rho_{j+1}=\rho_j-\beta_{j+1}$. For $\gamma\in\Psi_j\setminus\{\beta_{j+1}\}$, some other current simple-root coefficient is positive (the root system is reduced), and reflection in $\beta_{j+1}$ leaves that coefficient unchanged. Sign coherence therefore makes the reflected root positive; involutivity shows this reflection permutes $\Psi_j\setminus\{\beta_{j+1}\}$. It carries $\Psi_j$ onto $\Psi_{j+1}$, so it sends $\rho_j$ to $\rho_j-\beta_{j+1}$; the reflection formula gives $\langle\rho_j,\beta_{j+1}^\vee\rangle=1$. All these equalities are in the rational character space. Starting from the given integral $\rho$, the subtraction formula shows each $\rho_j$ is an actual character. Put $\mu_j=(q-1)\rho_j$; hence $\langle\mu_j,\beta_{j+1}^\vee\rangle=q-1$ as an integer.

source.place: Agent finite induction using root bases (C.21--C.22, p.612) and rank-one reflection (21.11, pp.428--430); adjacent-Borel existence and its positive roots are in the cited local lemma.

proof.text: Set $u_0=v$. Inductively suppose $u_j$ is a $\operatorname{Dist}(C_{j,r})$-eigenvector for the extension of $\mu_j$ trivial on $R_u(C_j)$. Apply the adjacent-Borel lemma to $V=M$, $C=C_j$, $\alpha=\beta_{j+1}$ and the root parametrizations specified in the item. Its integer-weight hypothesis was checked in step 2. It gives $u_{j+1}=d_{-\beta_{j+1}}^{(q-1)}u_j$, an eigenvector for $C_{j+1,r}$ of character $\mu_j-(q-1)\beta_{j+1}=\mu_{j+1}$, and $\kappa_{j+1}\in F^\times$ with $d_{\beta_{j+1}}^{(q-1)}u_{j+1}=\kappa_{j+1}u_j$. The base case is step 1. This proves the induction for $0\le j<N$.

source.place: Agent induction from the cited single-wall finite-kernel lemma; geometric rank-one setting is Milne 20.37--20.41 and 21.11.

proof.text: Write $E=d_{\beta_1}^{(q-1)}\cdots d_{\beta_N}^{(q-1)}$ and $F_-=d_{-\beta_N}^{(q-1)}\cdots d_{-\beta_1}^{(q-1)}$. By the defining recursion $u_N=F_-v$. Apply the recovery equations successively, starting with $d_{\beta_N}^{(q-1)}$ (the rightmost factor of $E$), then $d_{\beta_{N-1}}^{(q-1)}$, down to $d_{\beta_1}^{(q-1)}$. They yield $EF_-v=(\prod_{j=1}^N\kappa_j)v$. The product is a unit of $F$.

source.place: Agent multiplication of the recovery equations proved in step 3.

proof.text: Apply the unipotent Frobenius-distribution socle statement first to $R_u(B)$, using the enumerations $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_N$ and $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_N$, and then to the given opposite Borel's radical $U^-$, using $-\beta_N,\ldots,-\beta_1$ and $-\alpha_1,\ldots,-\alpha_N$. It says that each of the corresponding top products is nonzero and spans the same annihilator of the augmentation ideal. Consequently $E=a e_{\rm top}$ and $F_-=b f_{\rm top}$ for some $a,b\in F^\times$. These equalities also hold in $A$ under the distribution inclusions. Step 4 becomes $ab e_{\rm top}f_{\rm top}v=(\prod_j\kappa_j)v$, so $c=(ab)^{-1}\prod_j\kappa_j$ is the required nonzero scalar. The local lemma and the socle statement include every prime and every $r\ge1$, so no restriction on $p$, including $p=2$, entered.

source.place: Agent comparison of the one-dimensional socles supplied by the cited node; no unproved exchange of noncommuting root factors is made.
